blocks.text: The group includes sharks, skates, rays, and ratfishes. They have skeleton of cartilage. Their body is covered by placoid (tooth-like) scales, called denticles. They have jaws and biting mouthparts. The pectoral and pelvic fins are paired. There are two dorsal fins. They possess single-circuit heart with one atrium and one ventricle. There is a pair of small openings, called spiracle, behind eyes. These are used for breathing. They do not have swim bladder. Fertilization is internal.

blocks.alt: Three cartilaginous fishes in a row. Left: Skate fish, a dark diamond-shaped skate with a long thin tail. Middle: a shark in side view, labelled two dorsal fins, caudal fin, anal fin, pelvic fin, pectoral fin, gill slits and the spiracle, with a circle below enlarging the tooth-like denticles. Right: Ray fish, a sandy-brown spotted ray with a tail.
